newsitem.title: GREECE: TOP IRANIAN IN EU-BREAKING TRIP TO GREECE.
newsitem.headline: TOP IRANIAN IN EU-BREAKING TRIP TO GREECE.

text.p: Iranian Vice President Hassan Habibi began a three-day official visit to Athens on Tuesday, the highest level Iranian visit to a European Union capital since the Islamic revolution in Tehran 18 years ago.
Greek diplomats said Habibi's trip was seen as a signal that Tehran sought closer ties with the EU.
"Our doors with the EU were always open despite some political differences," Habibi told reporters after talks with Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
He said Greece and Iran had maintained close relations for many years and that working groups from both countries would meet in the next two days to push for stronger commercial ties.
Simitis said that the talks focused on Middle East, Black Sea and bilateral issues and that Athens and Tehran had similar views on many regional matters.
"The talks were very friendly and there could be joint action in many areas, for example in the Black Sea region," Simitis said.
Greece spends some $600 million a year on buying Iranian oil.
